assertions.name: jet_rank_0_derivation_q_independent_and_matches_textbook
assertions.unit: boolean — derivation gives π²/720 at all q tested
assertions.source: Tests the structural claim that Casimir = rank-0 observable, hence q-independent.  Passing this assertion confirms the jet-order derivation route is self-consistent.  Whether the rank-0 assignment is CORRECT is a separate physics question, but the assignment yields a forced (non-fit) result.

description: Derivation attempt under the jet-order axiom: Casimir lives at GB rank 0 (commutative substratum, no q-deformation).  This forces ε_n = n·ε (no [n]_q), which gives Σ n³ → ζ(-3) = -1/120 (standard ζ-regularization), yielding c_q = π²/720 EXACTLY at any q.  Test: evaluate the derived prefactor at three q values (1.05, substrate, 1.5).  If all three give π²/720, the derivation is q-independent (as required by the rank-0 hypothesis) and matches the textbook value.  This makes the jet-order route the FIRST candidate that's both derived (no q-deformation choice) AND matches standard Casimir at substrate.

verdict.interpretation: Under jet-rank-0 axiom, QOU Casimir = standard Casimir exactly at substrate.  No deviation predicted.  Sub-problem 3 RESOLVED via structural assignment (not fitting).
